candidateDecisions.label: Social Problems and Public Policy
candidateDecisions.assessment: Public economics, comparative constitutional law, policy analysis and communication support a coherent response to public problems and inequality.

candidateDecisions.label: Sociology of Digital Societies
candidateDecisions.assessment: Media history, AI ethics and sociological theory connect digital methods to social relationships and power. The technical courses support analysis without constituting a specialist social-network methods sequence.

analysis: The broad plan combines sociological theory, social psychology, organizations, inequality and political and economic institutions with statistics and qualitative and historical research. The historical seminar replaces negotiation and provides independent work on source-based questions. Family and neighborhood interests are supported through lifespan, social relationships and social theory rather than a dedicated family-demography or neighborhood methods sequence. Religious institutions and safety remain legitimate Utrecht interests; UCR contributes general sociological explanations and historical context, with no standalone specialization asserted. The digital plan integrates social theory and digital publics with media history, race, rhetoric, databases, AI ethics, programming and statistical learning. The policy plan uses public economics, comparative constitutional law, policy analysis, rights, environmental justice and communication. The added description-only Public Policy Analysis contributes a concrete cross-scale policy case and memo writing. The two focused plans retain common sociology and research while using distinct courses and analytical aims. The eight aligned rows cover substantive overlaps in social theory, methods, public policy, prejudice and organizations. Broader content is shown separately from specialized family demography, network analysis and evaluation. The technical digital courses do not provide a dedicated network-analysis course. The optional UCR independent research element remains separate from Utrecht’s required project.

alignment.rationale: Both introduce sociological concepts and theories for understanding institutions and social relationships.
Utrecht uses formal models to study social interaction. UCR examines a range of theoretical approaches in sociology.
Utrecht studies how social inequalities are measured and explained. UCR examines inequality in several courses, including environmental justice.
Utrecht studies explanations for a range of social problems. UCR approaches public problems through sociology, policy and law.
Utrecht introduces behavioral science through several disciplines. UCR introduces brain and behavior and studies social psychology.
Utrecht studies family formation and household relationships using quantitative research. UCR studies relationships and development across the lifespan.
Both introduce research design, measurement and statistical reasoning for empirical study.
Both apply statistical methods to data from social or behavioral research.
Both develop qualitative research design, interviewing and analysis through applied projects.
Both study prejudice and relations between social groups. UCR covers these within a broader social psychology course.
Both use data analysis in practical work. Utrecht emphasizes testing social-science hypotheses, while UCR develops broader data handling and visualization.
Both examine organizations, working relationships and the social processes that shape them. UCR also studies leadership.
Utrecht uses a supervised research practicum. UCR develops research experience in several courses.
Utrecht teaches dedicated social-network theory and research. UCR studies digital publics, media and relationships across courses.
Both examine how policies are made and how institutions shape public decisions.
Utrecht teaches policy evaluation as a dedicated research course. UCR studies public policy and econometric methods in separate courses.
Utrecht requires a 15 EC empirical research project. The UCR comparison shows optional independent research separately.
Choose 45 EC of eligible electives, including at least 15 EC at intermediate level or above.
